steps.title: AO4 (5-10%)
steps.body: covers spelling, punctuation, and structure. A well-organised essay scores higher.

steps.title: Top Tip
steps.body: Always spend 5 minutes planning before writing. A student with a strong plan and 3 well-structured paragraphs will outperform a student with 5 rambling paragraphs every time. Examiners reward coherent argument over quantity — structure is your roadmap to every mark.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What are the three parts of an essay? | What does PEEL stand for? | What should an introduction include?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Introduction, Body Paragraphs, Conclusion. Introduction sets up argument, body develops with evidence, conclusion summarises and evaluates. | Point - Make your argument. Evidence - Quote the text. Explain - Analyse the quotation. Link - Connect to question/theme/context. | Introduction should: identify text and writer, respond to the question, state your main argument (thesis). Keep it 2-3 sentences.
